title: 30th Celebration, seven weeks in
headline: Seven weeks in, the 30th Celebration's Pikachu promos led the list down.
dek: Over 25 mornings, Oct 9 to Nov 2, 13 cards from the 30th Celebration made the board's 7-day list 35 times, 33 of them down. Pikachu ex 107 made it 11 mornings, the most of any card in that span; the price the list showed for it went from $249.25 on Oct 13 to $115.60 on Nov 1. Pikachu ex 109 made it 7 mornings, from $232.65 to $112.75. The Classic Collection Lugia came back on Nov 2 at $156.21, down 20.4% in a week. None of the 250 rows the 7-day list published in those 25 mornings had a checked sale behind it.
why_now: This is the first hand-written File since Oct 8, when the board's first 7-day list showed four 30th Celebration cards falling on days 12 to 19 after the Sep 16 launch. The list has run every morning since, and from this week the board writes its own File on the days nobody does. Seven weeks in is long enough to ask what the list actually saw.
risk: A 7-day list shows a card only on the mornings it moved enough: Pikachu ex 107 was off it from Oct 22 to Oct 29, which means its week-over-week move was under 5% or failed the list's rule, not that the price held. The prices here are TCGplayer's market price on the mornings the card was listed, not a daily series, and the list's start-of-week prices are worked back from the rounded change. Unconfirmed means no sale was checked, not that anything is wrong. This is not a read on whether these prices are high or low.
what_to_watch: Whether the two Pikachu promos leave the list for the right reason, a week without a move, and whether Victini 102 keeps going: it has been on the since-yesterday list three mornings running, down 38.2%, 26.5% and 13.2%, to $23.32. The Oct 8 File's other cards: Jirachi ex and Gengar ex never came back to the 7-day list, and Mew ex 152 made it once more (Oct 9, down 38.5%) and the since-yesterday list six times, last up 11.3% on Nov 1. The label is what this File is missing: Mission Control is starting to store checked eBay sales for a short list of tracked cards, and the morning one of these cards has one, its row stops reading Unconfirmed.
source: TCGplayer market prices via tcgcsv.com, from the board's 7-day lists published Oct 9 to Nov 2, 2026 (prices Oct 8 to Nov 1) and the Nov 2 list (prices Oct 25 to Nov 1)

foot: Market price: TCGplayer's average of recent completed sales of the same card, condition and printing (help.tcgplayer.com). The three moves: the board's Nov 2 list, prices Oct 25 to Nov 1, 2026, the change between 3-day medians at each end; the start-of-week prices are worked back from the listed price and its rounded change, then rounded to the dollar, so within a dollar. The 25-morning counts: the board's own published 7-day lists, Oct 9 to Nov 2 (git history of data/movers.json), 10 rows a morning, 250 in all; a card counts once per morning it was listed. The listed price on a morning is TCGplayer's market price as of the day before. The list: up to 10 Pokémon cards worth $20 or more that moved 5% or more in a week; with no checked sales, a move shows only if it's 60% or less, the lowest listing moved the same way by at least a quarter as much, the price changed in the last 2 days, and the card trades (its price changed on 3 or more of the last 14 days). A card not on it may have moved less, more, or in a way the rule leaves out. Launch: Sep 16, 2026. Unconfirmed: no sale checked by Mission Control's Sale Integrity Layer in that window. Not advice.
